questions_and_answers.question_text: What does yíxià mean, and what does it indicate?
What does the use of yíxià communicate?
What would have communicated the same indefiniteness?
Does the first speaker commit himself to an exact length of time?
Write the Chinese for "Please stop at that bank up ahead for a moment."
Give the reduplicated form of tíng that would communicate the same thing.
Write the Chinese for "I'll park the car over there and wait for you."

answers.answer_text: Wǒ bǎ chē tíng zai nèibian děng nín.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which construction is used in the reply to bring the object forward?

answers.answer_text: The bǎ construction — Wǒ bǎ chē tíng…

articles.text:
10. A: Qǐng ni zài qiánbian nèige    Please stop at that bank up ahead
       yínháng tíng yíxià.            for a moment.
    B: Hǎo. Wǒ bǎ chē tíng zai        Okay. I'll park the car over there
       nèibian děng nín.              and wait for you.

Note on No. 10

Yíxià, "awhile," is used to indicate a short, indefinite amount of time. The use of this word communicates indefiniteness, just as reduplicating the verb would have done (tíngyitíng). The first speaker in this exchange does not commit himself to an exact length of time.
